children: New Zealand-based retailer Briscoe's latest update offers encouraging signals about underlying trading momentum, says Macquarie. Near-term earnings conversion remains the key challenge. Briscoe reported a 2% rise in 3Q sales to NZ$174.4 million. That was faster than the 0.3% growth achieved in 2Q. Briscoe now expects FY27 net profit of up to NZ$55 million. "We lower FY27 forecasts to reflect this guidance and reduce FY28 earnings to capture a slower recovery as operating headwinds persist, and transformation benefits take time to emerge," Macquarie says. Its FY27-29 EPS forecasts fall 4-9%. Macquarie retains a neutral call on Briscoe, and trims its price target by 4.3% to NZ$4.50/share. Briscoe is at NZ$4.26 early today. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
